newsitem.title: USA: ABMS makes big revision to U.S. copper rod data.
newsitem.headline: ABMS makes big revision to U.S. copper rod data.

text.p: American Bureau of Metals Statistics said it has substantially revised its copper rod report for the U.S. which now showed a huge increase in copper rod production and shipments, particularly during 1996.
One of the reporting companies was providing incorrect data during 1996 and into 1997, the ABMS said. Revision of these figures lead to the big changes.
But further revisions could be in the pipeline.

"As I have mentioned before, despite the improvements in the rod report, it is important to note that the work is not finished, and that efforts will continue to provide improve market transparency in the future," ABMS executive director Brian Simpson said in a letter to subscribers.
Some analysts use ABMS data to forecast copper market prices and consumption.
According to ABMS's new report, copper rod mill production in 1996 totaled 4.215 billion lbs of copper content, up from 3.797 billion in 1995.
Receipts at copper rod mills rose to 4.355 billion lbs in 1996, up from 3.860 billion in 1995.
Production of copper in rod in February this year totaled 363.053 million lbs, down from January's revised 374.816 million pounds.
Shipments of copper in rod in February totaled 364.608 million lbs, compared to January's revised 421.286 million.
Inventory at copper rod mills in February were 120.739 million lbs compared to a revised 122.040 million in January.
